concepts.name: Round robins: matches and points
concepts.description: Every pair meets once: nC2 matches (twice that home and away). Each match gives out a fixed number of points, so the table’s total is known before a ball is bowled, or tells you the draws.

concepts.name: Knockouts: matches, byes and the draw
concepts.description: Every match knocks one player out, so n players need n − 1 matches. Byes fill the draw up to the next power of 2, and two players can meet only when their blocks of the draw meet.

concepts.name: Qualification: the most points and still out
concepts.description: To find the most points a team can score and still miss the top k, let k + 1 teams beat the rest and share their own matches evenly; one more win than that is always enough.

concepts.name: Points tables and partial results
concepts.description: Rebuild results from a table: the total gives the draws, each team’s points split into 3 × wins + draws, and teams on 0 or full points fix their matches first.

concepts.name: Routes and schedules
concepts.description: Count shortest routes on a grid with C(east + north, east), or add up routes into each junction; find the shortest road route by settling the nearest town first; a round robin needs n − 1 days (n if n is odd).

formulas.title: Matches in a round robin
formulas.prompt: n teams each play every other team once. How many matches?
formulas.formula:
Matches = nC2 = n(n − 1) ÷ 2
Twice each (home and away): n(n − 1)
formulas.explanation: Each team plays n − 1 others; n(n − 1) counts every match from both sides, so halve it.
formulas.commonMistake: Answering n(n − 1) for a single round robin.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many matches do 12 teams play, each meeting every other once?

formulas.title: Total points in a league
formulas.prompt: In a round robin of m matches, how many points are given out in all?
formulas.formula:
Win 2, draw 1 each: total = 2m, always
Win 3, draw 1 each: total = 3m − draws
formulas.explanation: A decisive match gives out win + loss points; a draw gives 2 × draw. With 2-1-0 both are 2, so the total never changes; with 3-1-0 each draw gives one point less.
formulas.commonMistake: Taking 3 points off the total for each draw instead of 1.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In a 3-1-0 league of 10 matches, 2 were drawn. What is the points total?

formulas.title: Knockout tournament
formulas.prompt: n players play a knockout. How many matches, rounds and byes?
formulas.formula:
Matches = n − 1
Rounds = smallest r with 2^r ≥ n
Byes = 2^r − n (in the first round)
formulas.explanation: Each match puts exactly one player out, and all but the champion go out. Byes fill the empty places of the draw so that the second round is a power of 2.
formulas.example: 20 players: 19 matches, 2^5 = 32 so 5 rounds, 32 − 20 = 12 byes, (20 − 12) ÷ 2 = 4 first-round matches.
formulas.commonMistake: Taking byes as n minus the power of 2 below (20 − 16 = 4): that is the number of first-round matches.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A knockout has 45 players. How many byes, and how many matches in all?

formulas.title: Who can meet whom
formulas.prompt: Players are numbered 1 to 2^r down a knockout draw. In which round can two of them meet?
formulas.formula:
Round k is played inside blocks of 2^k places: 1–2, 3–4, … then 1–4, 5–8, …
They meet in the first round whose block holds both
formulas.explanation: A player who keeps winning has come through a block of 2^k places after round k, so two players meet when their blocks first merge.
formulas.example: Players 3 and 6 of 16: blocks of 4 are 1–4 and 5–8 (apart); the block of 8, 1–8, holds both: round 3, the semi-final.
formulas.commonMistake: Judging by the gap between the numbers (6 and 7 meet only in the semi-final, though they are next to each other).
formulas.applicationPrompt: In a draw of 32, in which round can players 9 and 16 meet?

formulas.title: Most points and still out
formulas.prompt: n teams, each pair meets once, no ties, w points a win; the top k qualify and ties go against you. What score can still miss out, and what score is safe?
formulas.formula:
Most points and still out = w × (n − k − 1 + ⌊k/2⌋)
Safe = that + w
formulas.explanation: k + 1 teams beat the other n − k − 1 and share their own matches as evenly as possible; the weakest of them has n − k − 1 + ⌊k/2⌋ wins and can still finish (k + 1)th.
formulas.example: 6 teams, top 4, 2 points a win: 2 × (6 − 4 − 1 + 2) = 6 points can miss out; 8 is safe.
formulas.commonMistake: Making only k teams strong: it takes k + 1 teams to push one out.
formulas.applicationPrompt: 8 teams, top 4, 2 points a win: what is the safe score?

formulas.title: Reading a points table
formulas.prompt: How do you turn a team’s points into its results?
formulas.formula:
Points = 3 × wins + draws (3-1-0)
Wins + draws + losses = matches played
Draws in the table = 3m − total
formulas.explanation: Each team’s points split into wins and draws in only a few ways; the total number of draws, and teams with only one split, decide the rest.
formulas.example: 7 points from 3 matches: 2 wins and 1 draw (the only way). 3 points: 1 win, or 3 draws.
formulas.commonMistake: Treating one point as one win.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A team has 5 points from 4 matches (3-1-0). What are its possible records?

formulas.title: Shortest routes on a grid
formulas.prompt: A place is a blocks east and b blocks north on a street grid. How many shortest routes lead there?
formulas.formula:
Routes = C(a + b, a)
Through a junction (x, y): C(x + y, x) × C(a − x + b − y, a − x)
formulas.explanation: Every shortest route is a + b blocks long, a of them east; choosing which ones gives the route.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding the two parts of a route through a junction instead of multiplying.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many shortest routes lead 4 blocks east and 4 blocks north?

formulas.title: Shortest road route
formulas.prompt: How do you find the shortest route through a road network?
formulas.formula:
Fix the start at 0 km
Repeat: fix the nearest unfixed town; update its neighbours (distance through it, if smaller)
formulas.explanation: This is Dijkstra’s method: a town is fixed only when no other route can reach it more cheaply.
formulas.example: A–C 4, C–B 2, A–B 7: B is fixed at 6 (through C), not 7.
formulas.commonMistake: Choosing the route with the fewest roads instead of the fewest kilometres.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A–B 5, B–D 4, A–C 2, C–D 8. What is the shortest A to D?

formulas.title: Fewest days for a round robin
formulas.prompt: No team may play twice in a day. How many days does a round robin of n teams need?
formulas.formula:
n even: n − 1 days
n odd: n days (one team rests each day)
formulas.explanation: At most ⌊n/2⌋ matches fit in a day, and the circle method (fix one team, rotate the rest) reaches that bound.
formulas.example: 6 teams: 15 matches, 3 a day, 5 days. 7 teams: 21 matches, 3 a day, 7 days.
formulas.commonMistake: Answering n − 1 for an odd number of teams.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many days do 10 teams need, playing every other team once?

formulas.title: Draws from the total
formulas.prompt: A 3-1-0 league has m matches and a points total T. How many draws were there?
formulas.explanation: A decisive match gives 3 points, a draw 2: each draw is one point short of 3m.
formulas.commonMistake: Using 2m − T (the 2-1-0 total, which never changes).

formulas.title: Start with 0 and full marks
formulas.prompt: Where do you start in a points table with missing results?
formulas.formula:
A team on 0 lost every match
A team on full points won every match
A total with one split (7 = 2W + 1D) is fixed
formulas.explanation: These teams leave no choice, so their matches are fixed and every other team’s total shrinks.
formulas.example: Assam 7, Bihar 5, Goa 4, Kerala 0: Kerala lost all three, so Bihar’s two draws were with Assam and Goa.
formulas.commonMistake: Trying cases before placing the forced results.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In a four-team 3-1-0 table a team has 9 points. What do you know at once?

formulas.title: Routes avoiding a junction
formulas.prompt: How many shortest grid routes avoid a closed junction?
formulas.formula: Avoiding = all routes − routes through it
formulas.explanation: Counting the routes through one point is easy (multiply two smaller counts); everything else avoids it.
formulas.commonMistake: Answering the routes through the junction.
formulas.applicationPrompt: 3 east, 3 north, closed at (1, 1). How many routes avoid it?

formulas.title: Add the routes in
formulas.prompt: How do you count routes on a map with closed roads or one-way streets?
formulas.formula:
Routes to a point = sum of the routes to the points one step before it
(or work backwards: routes from a point = sum over the next points)
formulas.explanation: Write the count at each junction, starting with 1 at the start; a closed junction gets 0.
formulas.example: One-way: P→Q, P→R, Q→R, Q→S, R→S, R→T, S→T. From T back: S 1, R 2, Q 3, P 5.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Grid 2 east, 2 north with the centre closed. How many routes?

levels.title: Counting What Adds Up
levels.description: Round robins, knockouts, points tables, qualification and routes.

blocks.title: Count what must add up
blocks.body: In a round robin of n teams every pair meets once, so there are nC2 matches: 4 teams play 6, 8 teams play 28. Each match gives out a fixed number of points (2 when a win is worth 2 and a draw 1 each; 3 or 2 with 3-1-0 scoring), so the total of the points table is known, or tells you how many matches were drawn. In a knockout every match puts one player out, so n players need n − 1 matches.

blocks.title: The counting rules
blocks.body:
Round robin: nC2 matches
3-1-0 total = 3 × matches − draws
Knockout: n − 1 matches, byes = next power of 2 − n
Grid routes: C(east + north, east)
blocks.caption: Write these totals down before you read the clues: they are what fix the unknowns.

blocks.title: A table that tells you every result
blocks.body: Assam 7, Bihar 5, Goa 4, Kerala 0 (3-1-0). Total 16 = 18 − 2, so 2 draws. Kerala lost all three. 7 = 2 wins + 1 draw, 5 = 1 win + 2 draws, 4 = 1 win + 1 draw. Bihar’s two draws cannot be with Kerala, so they were with Assam and Goa; Assam beat Goa and Kerala, Goa beat Kerala, Bihar beat Kerala.

blocks.title: The most points and still out
blocks.body: To keep a team with many points out of the top k, it needs k teams level with or above it. So make k + 1 teams strong: they beat everyone else and share their own matches as evenly as possible. Their weakest member is the highest score that can still miss out; one more win is always enough.
With 2-1-0 scoring the total is always twice the number of matches, so it cannot tell you the draws. With 3-1-0 it can: every draw takes exactly one point off 3 × matches.

levels.title: Set Rules
levels.description: Matches, points totals, knockouts, the draw, qualification, tables and routes.

levels.title: Matches, Byes and Routes
levels.description: Counting matches, byes, days and grid routes.

levels.title: Totals and Tables
levels.description: Draws from totals, the knockout draw, qualification and a points table.

levels.title: Full Sets
levels.description: Closed junctions, shortest roads, smudged tables and play-off cut-offs.

questions.question: In an inter-college kabaddi league in Madurai, 8 colleges take part and every college plays every other college exactly once. How many matches are played?
questions.explanation: A match is a pair of colleges, so the league has 8C2 = 8 × 7 ÷ 2 = 28 matches.
solutionSteps: That counts every match twice, once for each college: 56 ÷ 2 = 28.
questions.method: Matches in a round robin = nC2 = n(n − 1) ÷ 2.

hints.text: How many matches does one college play?
8 × 7 counts each match from both sides; halve it.

commonMistakes: Answering 56, counting each match twice.
Answering 7, the matches of a single college.

questions.question: 32 players enter a knockout chess tournament in Pune: a player who loses a game is out. How many games are needed to find the champion?
questions.explanation: Every game knocks out exactly one player. To leave one champion, 31 players must go out, so 31 games are played (16 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1).
solutionSteps: Or: one loser per game, and 32 − 1 = 31 losers.
questions.method: Knockout matches = n − 1.

hints.text: How many players does each game knock out?
Everyone except the champion loses exactly once.

commonMistakes: 32: counting the champion as a loser too.
16: only the first round. 5: the number of rounds, not games.

questions.question: 6 teams play a hockey league in which every team meets every other team twice, once at home and once away. How many matches are played?
questions.explanation: A single round robin of 6 teams has 6C2 = 15 matches; playing home and away doubles it to 30.
questions.method: Twice each: n(n − 1).

hints.text: How many matches if each pair met only once?
Each pair meets twice, so double it.

commonMistakes: Answering 15, forgetting the return matches.
Answering 60, doubling n(n − 1) again.

questions.question: A badminton knockout in Lucknow has 20 players. Some players get a bye in the first round so that the second round starts with a power of 2 players. How many byes are given?
questions.explanation: The next power of 2 above 20 is 32, so the draw has 32 places and 32 − 20 = 12 of them are empty: 12 byes. The other 8 players play 4 matches, and 12 + 4 = 16 start the second round.
solutionSteps: Next power of 2 at or above 20: 32.
Check: 8 players play 4 matches; 12 + 4 = 16 in round 2.
questions.method: Byes = next power of 2 − number of players.

hints.text: What is the smallest power of 2 that is at least 20?
Byes fill the empty places in a draw of that size.

commonMistakes: 4: 20 − 16, which is the number of first-round matches, not byes.
8: the players who do play in the first round. 16: the size of the second round.

questions.question: 5 teams play a cricket league in which each pair meets once. A win earns 2 points, a tie or no-result 1 point to each side, and a loss 0. However the matches turn out, how many points are given out in all?
questions.explanation: There are 5C2 = 10 matches, and every match gives out exactly 2 points (2 + 0, or 1 + 1), so the table always adds up to 20.
solutionSteps: Each match gives out 2 points either way.
questions.method: With 2-1-0 scoring, total = 2 × matches.

hints.text: How many points does one match give out if it has a winner? If it is tied?
Count the matches: 5C2.

commonMistakes: Answering 10, counting matches instead of points.
Answering 40, counting 2 points for each team in every match.

questions.question: The streets of Ravi’s town form a square grid. His school is 3 blocks east and 2 blocks north of his house, and he walks only east or north. How many different routes can he take?
questions.explanation: Every route is 5 blocks long with exactly 3 of them east, so a route is a choice of which 3 of the 5 blocks go east: C(5, 3) = 10.
questions.method: Shortest grid routes = C(east + north, east).

hints.text: Write a route as a word of E’s and N’s. How many letters, and how many E’s?
Count the ways to place 3 E’s among 5 letters.

commonMistakes: Answering 6 (3 × 2) or 5 (3 + 2).
Answering 20, counting each route once for each direction.

questions.question: 6 teams play a round robin in which each pair meets once, and no team plays more than one match on a day. What is the least number of days the league needs?
questions.explanation: There are 15 matches, and at most 3 fit in a day (6 teams, two to a match), so at least 15 ÷ 3 = 5 days are needed. The circle method (fix one team, rotate the others one place a day) fits them into exactly 5.
questions.method: An even number n of teams needs n − 1 days.

hints.text: How many matches can be played on one day if no team plays twice?
Divide the total matches by that.

commonMistakes: 6: thinking one team must rest each day (only for an odd number of teams).
15: one match a day. 3: the matches in a day, not the days.

questions.question: 6 teams play a football league in Kolkata in which each pair meets once: 3 points for a win, 1 point to each side for a draw and 0 for a loss. The final points table adds up to 41. How many matches were drawn?
questions.explanation: There are 6C2 = 15 matches. A match with a winner gives out 3 points and a draw only 2, so with no draws the total would be 45. Each draw takes one point off: 45 − 41 = 4 draws.
questions.method: With 3-1-0 scoring, draws = 3 × matches − total.

hints.text: How many points does a match give out when it has a winner? When it is drawn?
Start from the total with no draws, 3 × 15.

commonMistakes: Answering 11, the matches that had a winner.
Answering 2, taking 2 points off for each draw.

questions.question: In a 16-player table tennis knockout, the players are numbered 1 to 16 down the draw: 1 plays 2, 3 plays 4, and so on, and the winners of neighbouring matches meet in the next round. If both keep winning, in which round can player 3 meet player 6?
questions.explanation: After round 2 (the quarter-final) player 3 has come through places 1–4 and player 6 through places 5–8. Those two blocks meet in round 3, the semi-final.
solutionSteps: Quarter-final: the block 1–4 and the block 5–8 each produce one winner.
Semi-final: the winners of 1–4 and 5–8 meet.
questions.method: Two players meet in the first round whose block (2, 4, 8, … places) holds both.

hints.text: Whom can player 3 meet in round 1? In round 2?
Players 3 and 6 are in places 1–8 but not in the same block of 4.

commonMistakes: Quarter-final: thinking 3 and 6 are close enough to meet in round 2.
Final: thinking players in the top half never meet before the final.

questions.question: 6 teams play a kabaddi league: each pair meets once, a win earns 2 points, a loss 0, and no match can be tied. The top 4 teams go to the play-offs, and if teams finish level on points, the tie is broken against the team in question. What is the greatest number of points a team can score and still miss the play-offs?
questions.explanation: To miss the top 4, a team needs 4 others level with or above it, so make 5 teams strong. Each beats the sixth team (1 win) and they share their 10 matches among themselves evenly, 2 wins each: 3 wins, 6 points, for all five, and one of them is 5th on the tie-break. 8 points (4 wins) for five teams would need 20 wins, but only 15 matches are played.
solutionSteps: A team misses out if 4 others finish level or above: look at 5 strong teams.
Each beats the weakest team: 1 win; among themselves 10 matches, 2 wins each.
3 wins = 6 points each, so 6 can still miss out.
8 points for five teams needs 20 wins > 15 matches: impossible.
questions.method: k + 1 teams beat the rest and share their own matches evenly: 2 × (n − k − 1 + ⌊k/2⌋).

hints.text: How many teams must finish level with or above a team for it to miss the top 4?
Let 5 teams beat the sixth, and share their 10 matches among themselves evenly.

commonMistakes: Answering 8: five teams cannot all win 4 matches.
Answering 2: making only 4 teams strong. Forgetting the matches the strong teams play against each other.

questions.question: 6 teams play a volleyball league: each pair meets once, a win earns 2 points, a loss 0, and no match can be tied. The top 3 teams reach the final round, and if teams finish level on points, the tie is broken against the team in question. What is the least number of points that guarantees a team a place in the final round?
questions.explanation: First, 6 points can miss out: four teams can each beat the other two (2 wins) and split their own 6 matches 2, 2, 1, 1, so two of them have 3 wins (6 points) and one of those is 4th on the tie-break. With 8 points (4 wins), three other teams would also need 4 wins: 16 wins, but there are only 15 matches. So 8 is always enough.
solutionSteps: Four strong teams beat the other two: 2 wins each.
Their 6 matches split 2, 2, 1, 1: the last two have 3 wins = 6 points, and one can be 4th.
8 points: four teams with 4 wins need 16 wins > 15.
questions.method: Find the most points that can still miss out, then add one win.

hints.text: Can 6 points miss out? Try four strong teams.
With 8 points, could three other teams also reach 8? Count the wins needed.

commonMistakes: Answering 6, which can still miss out.
Answering 10, the score of a team that wins every match.

questions.question: What was the result of the match between Bihar and Goa?
questions.context: Four state teams, Assam, Bihar, Goa and Kerala, played a football round robin in Guwahati: each pair met once. A win earned 3 points, a draw 1 point to each team and a loss 0.
questions.explanation: The table adds up to 16; six matches with no draws would give 18, so there were 2 draws. Kerala, on 0, lost all three. Assam’s 7 can only be 2 wins and a draw, Bihar’s 5 only 1 win and 2 draws, Goa’s 4 only 1 win and 1 draw. Bihar’s two draws cannot be against Kerala, so they were against Assam and Goa: Bihar and Goa drew.
solutionSteps: Bihar’s draws were with Assam and Goa, so Bihar v Goa was drawn.
questions.method: Draws from the total, each team’s points as 3W + D, then place the forced results.

hints.text: How many points would six matches give with no draws?
Bihar has two draws. Which teams could they have been against?

commonMistakes: Choosing "cannot be determined" before splitting each total into wins and draws.
Choosing "Bihar won": Bihar’s only win was against Kerala, the team on 0.

questions.question: How many matches did Goa win?
questions.context: Four state teams, Assam, Bihar, Goa and Kerala, played a football round robin in Guwahati: each pair met once. A win earned 3 points, a draw 1 point to each team and a loss 0.
questions.explanation: Goa has 4 points from 3 matches. As 3 × wins + draws with at most 3 matches, 4 can only be 1 win and 1 draw (the win was against Kerala, who lost every match).
questions.method: Split the points into 3 × wins + draws.

hints.text: Write 4 as 3 × wins + draws.
Could Goa have 4 draws? How many matches did it play?

commonMistakes: Answering 4, reading points as wins.
Answering 2: two wins would already be 6 points.

questions.question: How many different routes can a van take from Ambattur to Guindy?
questions.context:
Delivery vans in Chennai may use only these one-way routes between hubs:
Ambattur → Anna Nagar
Ambattur → Vadapalani
Anna Nagar → Vadapalani
Anna Nagar → T. Nagar
Vadapalani → T. Nagar
Vadapalani → Guindy
T. Nagar → Guindy
questions.explanation: Work backwards from Guindy, adding the routes out of each hub: T. Nagar has 1 (straight to Guindy); Vadapalani has 2 (via T. Nagar, or direct); Anna Nagar has 2 + 1 = 3 (via Vadapalani or T. Nagar); Ambattur has 3 + 2 = 5.
solutionSteps: Vadapalani: to T. Nagar (1) or Guindy (1) = 2.
Anna Nagar: to Vadapalani (2) or T. Nagar (1) = 3.
Ambattur: to Anna Nagar (3) or Vadapalani (2) = 5.
questions.method: Routes from a hub = sum of the routes from the hubs its roads lead to.

hints.text: Which hubs have a road straight to Guindy?
Work backwards, adding up the routes out of each hub.

commonMistakes: Answering 7, the number of roads.
Answering 4, missing the route Ambattur → Anna Nagar → Vadapalani → Guindy or one like it.

questions.question: The roads of a colony in Jaipur form a square grid. Meena’s office is 4 blocks east and 3 blocks north of her home, and she walks only east or north. The junction 2 blocks east and 1 block north of her home is closed for repairs. How many different routes can she take?
questions.explanation: All shortest routes: C(7, 4) = 35. Routes through the closed junction: C(3, 2) = 3 ways to reach it, times C(4, 2) = 6 ways from it to the office, 18 in all. Avoiding it: 35 − 18 = 17.
solutionSteps: To the junction (2 east, 1 north): C(3, 2) = 3.
From it to the office (2 east, 2 north): C(4, 2) = 6.
questions.method: Routes avoiding a junction = all routes − routes through it.

hints.text: Count all the shortest routes first.
Count the routes through the closed junction: to it, times from it.

commonMistakes: Answering 18, the routes that pass the closed junction.
Answering 26, adding the two parts (3 + 6 = 9) instead of multiplying.

questions.question: What is the length of the shortest route from Alur to Hosur?
questions.context:
Roads between villages near Hosur (each can be used in both directions):
Alur – Belur: 7 km
Alur – Chandur: 4 km
Chandur – Belur: 2 km
Belur – Dharur: 5 km
Chandur – Dharur: 9 km
Dharur – Hosur: 3 km
Belur – Hosur: 10 km
questions.explanation: Settle the nearest villages first. From Alur: Chandur 4. Belur is 7 directly but 4 + 2 = 6 through Chandur. Dharur: 6 + 5 = 11 through Belur (Chandur gives 13). Hosur: 11 + 3 = 14 through Dharur (Belur gives 16). Shortest: Alur → Chandur → Belur → Dharur → Hosur, 14 km.
questions.method: Fix the nearest village each time and update its neighbours.

hints.text: Is the direct road Alur – Belur the shortest way to Belur?
Find the shortest distance to Belur and to Dharur before Hosur.

commonMistakes: 17 km: the route with the fewest roads, Alur → Belur → Hosur.
15 km: using the direct road Alur – Belur. 16 km: going Chandur → Dharur, or Belur → Hosur directly.

questions.question: 5 teams play a football league: each pair meets once, with 3 points for a win, 1 point to each side for a draw and 0 for a loss. Only the top 2 reach the final, and if teams finish level on points, the tie is broken against the team in question. What is the greatest number of points a team can score and still miss the final?
questions.explanation: A team misses the final if 2 others finish level with or above it, so make 3 teams strong. Each beats the other two teams (6 points) and they beat each other in a circle (A beats B, B beats C, C beats A), 3 more each: 9 points for all three, and one is 3rd. They cannot all reach 10: their 3 matches among themselves give at most 9 points in all, so the three totals add up to at most 18 + 9 = 27.
solutionSteps: Three strong teams beat the other two: 6 points each.
A circle of wins among the three: 3 more each, 9 points.
Their matches give at most 27 points in all, so all three cannot reach 10.
questions.method: Make k + 1 teams strong; share their own matches so that the weakest scores as much as possible.

hints.text: How many teams must finish level with or above a team for it to miss the top 2?
Among three teams, which gives more points each: three draws, or a circle of wins?

commonMistakes: Answering 8: drawing all three matches among the strong teams gives only 2 points each from them, less than a circle of wins.
Answering 12, the score of a team that wins every match.

questions.question: Which of these must be true? Select all that apply.
questions.context: Five hockey teams, Odisha, Punjab, Haryana, Jharkhand and Karnataka, played a round robin in Bhubaneswar: each pair met once, with 3 points for a win, 1 point to each team for a draw and 0 for a loss. Exactly 3 matches were drawn. Jharkhand’s total in the final table has been smudged.

options.text: Odisha did not lose a match.
Jharkhand drew two of its matches.

questions.explanation: Ten matches with 3 draws give 30 − 3 = 27 points, so Jharkhand has 27 − 22 = 5. Odisha’s 10 from 4 matches can only be 3 wins and a draw, so it is unbeaten. A team on 4 has 1 win and 1 draw (4 draws would need 4 drawn matches, but there are only 3), so Karnataka won exactly one. Jharkhand’s 5 is 1 win and 2 draws. Who Odisha drew with, and how Punjab v Haryana went, can be arranged in more than one way that fits the table.
solutionSteps: Odisha’s draw and Punjab v Haryana are not fixed.

questions.question: A knockout tennis tournament in Chandigarh has 24 players. Byes are given in the first round so that the second round starts with a power of 2 players. Which of these are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: 12 matches are played in the first round.

questions.explanation: Every match knocks out one player, so 24 − 1 = 23 matches. The draw has 32 places (2^5), so 32 − 24 = 8 byes and 5 rounds. The other 16 players play 8 first-round matches, not 12.
questions.method: Matches n − 1; rounds and byes from the next power of 2.

hints.text: What is the smallest power of 2 that is at least 24?
How many players actually play in the first round?

commonMistakes: Selecting 12 first-round matches: that ignores the 8 byes.
Selecting 6 rounds: 2^5 = 32 is already enough.

questions.question: How many points did Jharkhand score?
questions.context: Five hockey teams, Odisha, Punjab, Haryana, Jharkhand and Karnataka, played a round robin in Bhubaneswar: each pair met once, with 3 points for a win, 1 point to each team for a draw and 0 for a loss. Exactly 3 matches were drawn. Jharkhand’s total in the final table has been smudged.
questions.explanation: There are 5C2 = 10 matches. With 3 draws the table adds up to 3 × 10 − 3 = 27. The other teams have 10 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 22, so Jharkhand has 27 − 22 = 5.
questions.method: Total points = 3 × matches − draws.

hints.text: How many matches did five teams play in all?
Each draw gives out one point less than a win.

commonMistakes: Answering 8, using 30 as the total and forgetting the draws.
Answering 2, taking 3 points off for each draw.

questions.question: 9 teams play a basketball league in Bengaluru in which every team meets every other team twice, and no team plays more than one match on a day. What is the least number of days the league needs?
questions.explanation: There are 2 × 9C2 = 72 matches. With 9 teams at most 4 matches fit in a day (one team always rests), so at least 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days are needed. Each round robin fits in 9 days by the circle method, so 18 days is enough.
solutionSteps: Days ≥ 72 ÷ 4 = 18; two 9-day round robins reach it.
questions.method: An odd number n of teams needs n days per round robin.

hints.text: How many matches can be played on a day when one team must rest?
Count all the matches of both round robins.

commonMistakes: Answering 16: 2 × (9 − 1), forgetting that one team rests each day.
Answering 9: only one round robin.
